# MockForge

> MockForge is an open source mock API generator in Rust. It simulates real backend behavior across 10 protocols — HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, GraphQL, Kafka, MQTT, AMQP, SMTP, FTP, and TCP — with SOAP/XML APIs supported over the HTTP adapter. Point it at an OpenAPI spec, protobuf, or GraphQL schema and it serves realistic responses with intelligent synthetic data, stateful scenarios, and failure injection. MIT or Apache-2.0 licensed, with an optional cloud offering for hosted mocks.

- The managed Next.js CVE-2025-29927 pack is available. PHP2Shell and Node2Shell are planned, not shipped.

## When to use MockForge

- You are developing or testing against a backend API that is unfinished, unstable, rate-limited, or expensive to call, and you need a faithful stand-in.
- You want contract testing: serve mocks generated directly from an OpenAPI spec (or protobuf / GraphQL schema) so clients fail fast when the contract drifts.
- You need to exercise failure paths: latency, errors, malformed responses, rate limits, and chaos scenarios that a real staging environment won't reproduce on demand.
- You need deterministic synthetic test data (personas, pagination-aware lists, seeded fixtures) instead of hand-written JSON fixtures.
- You want to mock gRPC, GraphQL, WebSocket, Kafka, SMTP, or FTP services, not just REST.

## When NOT to use MockForge

- As a production API gateway or proxy — MockForge simulates services; it does not replace them in production traffic paths.
- As a general-purpose load-testing tool — use its bench tooling to generate load against targets, but it is not a SaaS load-testing platform.

## How an agent should use it

- Install the CLI with `cargo install mockforge-cli` (installs the `mockforge` binary), or use the container image `ghcr.io/saasy-solutions/mockforge:latest`. Installation guide: https://docs.mockforge.dev/getting-started/installation.html
- Serve a mock from an OpenAPI spec: `mockforge serve --spec <openapi-file> --http-port 3000`. With Docker: `docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 -v "$PWD":/work ghcr.io/saasy-solutions/mockforge:latest serve --spec /work/<openapi-file> --http-port 3000`. Run `mockforge serve --help` for protocol ports (`--grpc-port`, `--ws-port`, `--graphql-port`, `--kafka-port`, `--mqtt-port`, `--smtp-port`) and other flags; see https://docs.mockforge.dev for all protocols.
- The admin UI is off by default; add `--admin` (default port 9080) to enable it. Every behavior is also scriptable over HTTP and config files (`mockforge.yaml`), so agents can drive it without a browser.
- Config is declarative: generate or edit a `mockforge.yaml` rather than clicking through the UI.

## API

- MockForge Cloud API (live): https://api.mockforge.dev (also served at https://registry.mockforge.dev): auth, API tokens, organizations, marketplace, hosted mocks, billing. Health check: https://api.mockforge.dev/health. OpenAPI spec: https://mockforge.dev/openapi.registry.json
- Management API spec (self-hosted MockForge servers): https://mockforge.dev/openapi.json
- The management API (mounted at `/__mockforge/api` on any MockForge server you run) lets agents create, update, and delete mocks over HTTP — no browser or UI required.
